topic: How Multilayer Perceptrons (MLP) Store Facts in Transformers
target_audience: University students with a basic background in linear algebra and neural networks.

sections.title: The Analogy: The Brain vs. The Bookshelf
lecture_lines: Transformers use Attention and MLP layers.
Attention is the index for information.
animations: Display bookshelf icon #FFFFFF and brain icon #FF00FF.
Show brain accessing bookshelf with a glowing connection #FFFF00.
Flash brain icon #FF00FF to signify memory retrieval.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Concept of Key-Value Memories
animations: Write 'Key: Fact' in #00FFFF and 'Value: Data' in #00FF00.
Connect Key and Value with an arrow #FFFFFF.
Flash the connection arrow #FFFFFF to emphasize link.

sections.title: Mechanism: The Projection and Activation Cycle
lecture_lines: Input vectors project into high-dimensional space.
Facts exist as distinct vector directions.
animations: Show input vector as dot #FF9900 moving toward grid.
Animate grid transformation #00FFFF to project vector.
Highlight resulting activation pattern with yellow pulse #FFFF00.
Move activation through layers with trail effect #FFFFFF.
Fade output result onto screen in #00FF00.

sections.title: Updating Knowledge: Fact Editing and Superposition
lecture_lines: Multiple facts overlap in neural space.
We update facts by re-weighting vectors.
animations: Modify color of cell to #00FF00 to show update.

sections.title: Synthesis and Summary
lecture_lines: MLPs function as compressed distributed databases.
They do not search database tables.
They reconstruct facts from learned patterns.
